experiment.answers: the claim boundary of ACCELERATOR_GATE_DISAGREEMENT.json in its own words -- 'says how fast a subsample approaches 176 rows, NOT whether 176 is enough'

headline: BOTH KNOBS I REACHED FOR ARE THE WRONG ONES. 176 rows agrees with a 1518-row pooled capture on 98.7% of packs -- prediction confirmed -- but NOT because 176 is enough: 512 rows is NO BETTER (1.39% flip against 176's 1.27%). And the calibration DOMAIN barely matters, refuting my own prediction. ALL the instability, from sampling AND from domain, lives in packs with under 0.002 of headroom: those flip on 20.8% of resamples while packs beyond 0.01 flip on NONE and never disagree across any domain. HEADROOM IS THE VARIABLE.

the_banding_is_the_result.reading: 4 packs of 72 carry a 20.8% flip rate; the 43 in the middle band carry 0.19%; the 25 beyond 0.01 carry ZERO and no domain ever disagrees about them. This is not a gradient, it is a cliff, and it explains BOTH measurements at once.
the_banding_is_the_result.why: the mean cosine gap keeps falling with N (0.00103 at 64, 0.00038 at 176, 0.00018 at 512) while the FLIP RATE does not, because a flip needs the estimate to cross a threshold and the packs that cross are the ones sitting on it. Sampling error shrinks; the distance to the bar does not.
the_banding_is_the_result.small_n_stated: the 20.8% rests on 4 packs x 12 resamples = 48 draws

prediction_a_confirmed_for_the_wrong_rea.written: 176 rows agrees with the pooled answer on >=95% of packs
prediction_a_confirmed_for_the_wrong_rea.measured: 98.7% (flip rate 1.27% over 72 packs against a 1518-row pooled capture)
prediction_a_confirmed_for_the_wrong_rea.verdict: CONFIRMED, and the reasoning behind it was wrong -- I expected agreement to come from 176 being a sufficient sample, and it comes from 68 of 72 packs being so far from the threshold that any N decides them

prediction_b_refuted.written: domain changes >=5% of verdicts, and the dangerous direction is a narrow domain ACCEPTING what the pool rejects
prediction_b_refuted.verdict: REFUTED IN BOTH HALVES. Mean disagreement 2.6%; only multilingual reaches the 5% bar at 5.56% and code disagrees on NOTHING. And the direction is symmetric -- 4 domains accept one pack the pool rejects while 3 of them also reject packs the pool accepts, multilingual rejecting 3. Only 5 of 72 packs see any inter-domain disagreement at all, and 4 of those 5 sit in the tightest headroom band.
prediction_b_refuted.what_it_does_not_say: this measures ONE small encoder whose activations may be less domain-sensitive than a decoder's. It is evidence against my prediction, not a licence to calibrate on whatever text is nearest.

the_float32_bar_was_28x_too_optimistic.reading: near_threshold_headroom already reported safe_at_float32 at 100x the measured 2.85e-06 float32 disagreement = 2.85e-04. THREE OF SIX unstable packs PASS that bar, one of them flipping on 8.3% of 176-row resamples at headroom 0.00632 and another disagreeing across domains at 0.00815. When the gate's inputs are a SAMPLE, arithmetic precision is not the widest source of disagreement and was being reported as if it were.

shipped.near_threshold_headroom.decided_under_re: at a 0.002 bar, where the flip rate collapses from 20.8% to 0.19%
shipped.why_the_bar_is_not_at_the_widest_unstabl: cosine headroom for an ACCEPTED pack is capped at 1 - min_cosine, so a 0.01 bar with min_cosine 0.99 would call EVERY acceptance undecided -- a bar that refuses everything is not a safer bar. Pinned by a test so nobody tightens it into vacuity.
shipped.and_it_is_labelled_an_indicator: 2 of 72 packs above the bar were still unstable, and the field says so rather than reading as a guarantee

the_lake_sweep_landed_and_it_saturates_e.reading: at 4 bits / group 64 ELEVEN organs across FOUR architectures -- a sparse MoE decoder, its VL variant, a Mamba hybrid and a different MoE -- span 0.00105 of cosine. The weight-space number is nearly invariant not only across organs but across ARCHITECTURES, which is the strongest form of the previous block's finding that it measures the distribution's scale.
the_lake_sweep_landed_and_it_saturates_e.prediction_from_two_blocks_ago_now_settl: 'a setting adequate for one architecture's MLP is adequate for another's' -- CONFIRMED under this metric, and the confirmation is nearly worthless because the metric cannot distinguish them in the first place

a_defect_in_my_own_probe_and_i_blamed_th.what_happened: the sweep ran 40 minutes without printing a line and I attributed it to the USB volume, which a dd measurement showed delivering 0.22-0.42 MB/s under an unrelated filler writing 25-43 MB/s
a_defect_in_my_own_probe_and_i_blamed_th.the_actual_defect: safetensors framework='np' CANNOT READ bf16 -- 'data type bfloat16 not understood' -- and these shards are all bf16. My loader would have raised on EVERY tensor, inside a broad except that recorded the error and printed NOTHING.
a_defect_in_my_own_probe_and_i_blamed_th.how_it_was_found: a single bounded probe on ONE tensor, which also showed the index and open costing 5.24 s and 2.77 s -- not the wall I had been assuming
a_defect_in_my_own_probe_and_i_blamed_th.what_is_and_is_not_established: the bf16 defect is CERTAIN, demonstrated. Whether the 40-minute stall was I/O is NOT established -- the process sat in uninterruptible disk wait with 1.08 s of CPU, which points at I/O, and the fixed run completed in ~5 minutes with per-tensor loads of 2.9 to 65 s. Both were probably true and only one of them was measured.
a_defect_in_my_own_probe_and_i_blamed_th.lesson_recorded: a broad except around an I/O call makes a TYPE error look like a SLOW disk, and the environment was blamed for a bug in the probe

claim_boundary.activations_from_one_model: MiniLM only; the four lake specimens are graded in WEIGHT space because no runtime here executes a Qwen3-MoE, Falcon or Mamba forward pass
claim_boundary.the_bar_rests_on_72_packs_of_one_model: 0.002 is where THIS model's flip rate collapses; it is not measured elsewhere
claim_boundary.domains_are_10_sentences_each: 1518 pooled rows from 50 sentences across 5 domains -- enough to show the domains mostly AGREE, not enough to characterise any one of them
claim_boundary.still_a_proxy: one layer's output cosine is not coherence

AMENDED_IN_PLACE_2026_08_25.what_is_corrected: this receipt justified weight-space grading with 'no runtime here executes a Qwen3-MoE, Falcon or Mamba forward pass'. THAT CONFLATES TWO RUNTIMES. Hawking's Rust body dispatches only on llama/mistral/qwen2 families and really does cover none of them; mlx_lm 0.31.3 -- already a hard dependency and the runtime every AIR kernel executes through -- carries model classes for qwen3_moe, qwen3_vl_moe, kimi_vl AND falcon_h1.
AMENDED_IN_PLACE_2026_08_25.what_the_gate_actually_is: FAST LOCAL STORAGE. Falcon-H1-7B, the smallest specimen, is 15.17 GB and under the operator-prioritised fill a sequential read did not complete 256 MiB in 120 s -- under ~0.5 MB/s against 96-131 MiB/s uncontended.
AMENDED_IN_PLACE_2026_08_25.what_does_NOT_change: every weight-space caveat here stands. No forward pass was run and no activations exist for any lake specimen; what changes is the REMEDIATION -- a quiesced window rather than writing a reader.
